# Didache Chapter 13 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 13

---

## Chapter 13

**1** Every genuine prophet who wishes to settle among you is worthy of his sustenance.

**2** Similarly, a genuine teacher is worthy of his sustenance, just as a worker is.

**3** Take the firstfruits of every produce of the wine-press and the threshing floor, of cattle and sheep, and give them to the prophets — for they are your high priests.

**4** But if you have no prophet, give them to the poor.

**5** When you bake bread, take the firstfruits and give in accordance with the commandment.

**6** Similarly, when you open a jar of wine or oil, take the firstfruits and give to the prophets.

**7** Take the firstfruits of money, clothing, and every possession — as much as seems appropriate to you — and give in accordance with the commandment.

---

### Council Notes

**On ἀρχιερεῖς — "chief priests" vs. "high priests":** EMET uses "chief priests," LOGOS and PNEUMA use "high priests." ἀρχιερεῖς in the LXX refers to the high priest (Aaron and his successors) and, by extension in the NT, to the chief priestly families. Here, given the explicit analogy to the Levitical firstfruits system, "high priests" is the more theologically appropriate rendering — the prophets stand in the position of the Aaronic priesthood.
**Ruling:** "High priests" (LOGOS/PNEUMA) adopted.

**On "food" vs. "sustenance":** EMET's "food" (τροφή) is literal; LOGOS's "sustenance" is slightly broader and implies ongoing support beyond meals. Since prophets are settling long-term (v.1), "sustenance" is more fitting.
**Ruling:** "Sustenance" (LOGOS) adopted for vv. 1-2.

**On v.7 ("as much as seems appropriate to you"):** All agents agree this clause grants the giver discretion in giving of money and possessions — unlike the produce firstfruits (which have fixed proportions from Torah). The community can determine what "firstfruits" of cash means for themselves. This is a pastoral accommodation.
